question: Should Dreaming scoping land as plugin-owned `plugins.entries.memory-core.config.dreaming.agents`, per-agent `agents.list[].dreaming`, or a split where opt-out/allowlist lands now and schedules/staggering wait?
rationale: The request adds new user configuration and changes which agent memory artifacts receive Dreaming writes, so repository policy and VISION.md make this an explicit product/API compatibility choice rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Prefer plugin allowlist first
options.body: Use the https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100057 shape as the likely owner-boundary fit, then split per-agent schedules or stagger behavior into a follow-up if still needed.

options.title: Continue per-agent config
options.body: Use the https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/67420 shape if maintainers want Dreaming controls to live directly on agent entries despite expanding the core agent config surface.

options.title: Pause for pressure/backoff design
options.body: Keep the issue open without landing new config until maintainers decide whether memory pressure gates or cron staggering should be the primary product solution.

recommendation.title: Prefer plugin allowlist first
recommendation.body: Use the https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100057 shape as the likely owner-boundary fit, then split per-agent schedules or stagger behavior into a follow-up if still needed.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Dreaming resolver/runtime commits make steipete the strongest routing candidate for the API and owner-boundary decision.
